sections.value:
**Security: block**, round-two delta at `ef598b5437ef6a5578a2e478f358736a2e1226a4`, against `f105c6c1547307c12ee760e7ea69772c0b38e687` (output `69f67803aed4ae10657f840a60bad5351f6e2461`), under C33.

The orphan notice body repairs hold, including S197-002's fallback diagnostics. S197-001 remains partially open at actual Telegram presentation: the worker adds an unrendered owner/folder prefix before the repaired body. PM confirmed this inherited helper is on #197's own output path and must be repaired here.

| # | Severity | File | Lines | Vulnerability | Confidence |
|---|----------|------|-------|---------------|------------|
| 1 | 🟡 MEDIUM | crates/sidecars/src/telegram.rs; crates/daemon/src/background.rs | 720-731, 1261-1280; 1711-1718 | S197-001: final Telegram formatting reintroduces raw owner identity and recorded folder context ahead of the safe notice | 9/10 |

## Remaining presentation path

The changed orphan flow correctly renders the owner inside its notice, fences the log path, and renders/fences the prime and fallback reasons. It also correctly preserves the original `job.owner` when calling `routing.telegram`: routing and reply-binding keys must remain the real data, not a display label.

`DaemonColdRouting::telegram` places that raw identity in `TelegramSend.from` (`daemon/src/bg_routing.rs:143-153`). Production Telegram processing fetches optional recorded folder context and passes both values to `prefixed_text_parts`.

That formatter builds `[{from}] [{context}]` directly. A forged legacy owner therefore produces raw line breaks or framing **before** the safe orphan body. Missing registry rows remove folder context but do not protect the identity. A recorded folder basename can likewise introduce confusing text.

The new forged-field test captures `FakeRouting`'s body; it never exercises this final prefix. Body assertions cannot certify the actual transmitted payload.

Keep raw identities for routing, but grammar-render the worker's displayed owner and fence its displayed folder context. Test the hostile-field case through real Telegram formatting. This is safe rendering for readers under C33, not an account-isolation or sender-credential demand.

## Repairs and external content

S197-001's original owner/path interpolation **inside the body** is repaired. S197-002's generation paths render displayed seats and fence refusal/error diagnostics. The current regression covers hostile owner/path and gone-prime text, not a hostile refusal/error through the real worker.

The orphan payload contains title, job id/outcome, owner, absence duration/classification, quoted log path and routing explanation. It exports no command, event contents, capability token or log-tail contents. Locally assembling a completion body does not make that body the orphan payload.

The worker restricts egress to the configured operator chat; its production API default is HTTPS. No unauthorized destination or actual secret disclosure was established. Fencing is not secret redaction, and raw structured data remains untrusted.

**C33: same-user, out of scope** — local id reservations, local forged claims, operator-environment manipulation and local adversarial races are not blockers.

## Replay and correctness limits

The source supports the specified repairs: saved settlement precedes owner reclassification; an admitted prime leg completes without owner redelivery or extra Telegram; an unadmitted recorded prime is rechecked for warmth; and cold/gone fallback is recorded. Failed settlement retains the 60-second brake, with parameter-bound exclusions in the pending query.

Telegram commitment precedes enqueue. The expressly stated crash window can lose one notification between those writes; this is not guaranteed delivery. Neither commitment nor queue admission proves exactly-once Telegram network delivery, because the existing worker can retry an ambiguous send.

One separate **correctness handoff**, not an unauthorized-disclosure finding: `background.rs:1688-1699` treats every `accept()` error as failed admission. `delivery/mod.rs:1463-1487` can return `DeliveryAuditFailed` after admission/delivery. That can produce both prime delivery and Telegram fallback despite the pre-send `admitted` check. Recheck admission after ambiguous errors before changing route. This was sent to PM for correctness grading; it is not an additional C33 security block.

## CI and receipts

Exact local/remote/GitHub heads agree; detached shared worktree clean; PR CLEAN. The own delta is the single `ef598b54` commit.

CI [42549951858](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42549951858) tested merge `3b1829f5d1284402ad32ddc73a5f7e9cb661a762`, with this head and actual main `033b36f60a3a53a51aea761ee2de42345b54d842` as parents; tree `7f2bf64299ad8b0c9f5101cfc052385ba63332f1`. The relevant reviewed/traced source files are unchanged in that tested composition.

JUnit artifact [13644099523](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42549951858/artifacts/13644099523) confirms 2,316 passing cases, no failures; five separately skipped. All seven new replay/brake/forged-body cases executed, along with original grace/settlement/revive cases.

The supplied mutation receipts record R2-M1-M7 and brake/grace applications, killing failures, restoration comparisons and a final gate. They were read, not independently rerun. These are fixture/failpoint executions, not actual daemon crashes or final-worker hostile rendering proof.

No local builds/tests, mutations, live/Telegram probes, credential reads or product edits.
